questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Tissue is classified as adipose connective tissue when the majority of the cells that compose the tissue are adipocytes. Adipocytes can also occur singly or in small clusters in other tissues.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Dense irregular connective tissue has relatively few cells; those that are present are nearly all fibroblasts, many of which are inactive. In addition, the tissue has large-caliber collagen bundles, which have no organized arrangement.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The majority of the chromatin in the nucleus of these fibroblasts is highly condensed and, thus, the cells are metabolically inactive. The condensed chromatin stains intensely with hematoxylin. Inactive fibroblasts have minimal cytoplasm and thin processes.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structure indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Collagen bundles are large, greater than five microns, and are composed of many collagen fibrils. Collagen fibers are eosinophilic and inelastic.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Mast cells have large numbers of uniformly sized granules in their cytoplasm, which can stain with either hematoxylin or eosin depending on the contents of the granule. The nucleus is spherical and can either be located in the center of the cell or toward the periphery.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue that fills the field

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Dense regular connective tissue is exclusively found in tendons and ligaments and displays a parallel arrangement of collagen bundles. Inactive fibroblasts are arranged in rows between the bundles of collagen.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. This tissue is classified as adipose connective tissue and is composed of adipocytes. Distinctive features of adipocytes are an empty-appearing cytoplasm, due to the loss of the large lipid droplet during tissue processing, and the "signet ring" appearance of the cytoplasm and nucleus, which are displaced by the lipid droplet.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Loose connective tissue generally contains large numbers of cells of varying types. Furthermore, the collagen fibers are of much smaller caliber than the collagen bundles present in the dense connective tissues.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows in these images .

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Macrophages are the next most common cell present in connective tissue, after fibroblasts. Macrophages have an oval nucleus, which is smaller than that of an active fibroblast, prominent heterochromatin located adjacent to the nuclear envelope, and an indentation in the nuclear envelope, reflecting its origin from a monocyte.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells whose nuclei are indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The chromatin in the nucleus of these fibroblasts is highly dispersed and, thus, the cell is metabolically active. The dispersed chromatin binds hematoxylin at low density, resulting in the pale staining of the nucleus. In general, the nucleus of an active fibroblast is the largest nucleus seen in connective tissues.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. At the electron microscopic level, collagen fibrils can be resolved with their characteristic banding pattern. These fibrils can assemble into larger fibers and collagen bundles in the dense connective tissues.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cell indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Mast cells have large numbers of granules in their cytoplasm, which are clearly seen in this electron micrograph. The nucleus is spherical and can be located in the center or the periphery of the cell.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Plasma cells are distinguished by a 'clock-face' arrangement of heterochromatin around the nuclear envelope and a prominent 'negative Golgi' image near the nucleus. The well-developed Golgi membranes do not stain and, therefore, this region appears pale. The peripheral cytoplasm of plasma cells is highly basophilic, due to the large amount of rough endoplasmic reticulum.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the structures indicated by the arrows.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Elastic fibers are present in both loose and dense connective tissues, where they can be distinguished from collagen fibers by their higher electron density and amorphous appearance. The majority of the fiber is composed of elastin protein and the entire fiber is surrounded by microfibrils composed of fibrillin protein.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells shown in these images.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Eosinophils are granular white blood cells that migrate into connective tissues from the blood stream. They are phagocytic and function in parasitic infections. An eosinophil has intensely eosinophilic granules in its cytoplasm and a bilobed nucleus.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells shown in these images

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Lymphocytes, small, spherical cells with minimal cytoplasm, have rounded, very heterochromatic nuclei. Lymphocytes are agranular white blood cells transported via the blood, but are active only after entering connective tissue. Lymphocytes function in the immune response; some differentiate into plasma cells and produce antibodies.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cells shown in these images

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Neutrophils, or polymorphonuclear (PMN) leucocytes, are highly motile, phagocytic white blood cells that migrate from the blood to sites of tissue damage and infection. Each cell has a distinctive, 3-5 lobed nucleus. Its numerous granules are not visible with hematoxylin and eosin staining.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue shown in these images

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Mucous connective tissue is composed of fibroblast-like cells, which can be spindle or stellate shaped. They produce the surrounding, abundant, gelatinous ground substance (Wharton's jelly) and delicate collagen and reticular fibers.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Dense irregular connective tissue has relatively few cells, mostly inactive fibroblasts. In addition, the tissue has large-caliber collagen bundles in an irregular arrangement. A layer of loose connective lies just above this tissue beneath the epithelium.

questoes.enunciado: Classify the tissue that fills the field.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Reticular connective tissue is composed of a meshwork of reticular fibers that forms the stroma for hemopoietic tissues and lymphoid structures and organs, except the thymus. Reticular fibers are composed of collagen type III and are unique from Type I collagen fibers in that they branch and require special stains to be identified; silver (seen here) or periodic acid Schiff (PAS).

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cell whose nucleus is indicated by the double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. The chromatin in the nucleus of this inactive fibroblast is highly condensed and, thus, the cell is metabolically inactive. The condensed chromatin binds a high density of the heavy metals used for electron microscopy staining which which results in the high electron density of heterochromatin.

questoes.enunciado: Identify the cell indicated by double arrow.

alternativas.feedback: CORRECT. Macrophages are the major phagocytic cell in connective tissue. The macrophage nucleus has a prominent indentation, reflective of its origin as a monocyte, and accumulations of heterochromatin beneath the nuclear envelope. Macrophages process, folds and plasma membrane ruffling are prominent. Numerous heterogeneous lysosomes are also visible.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: CORRECT.  Tissue is classified as adipose connective tissue when the majority of the cells that compose the tissue are adipocytes.  Adipocytes can also occur singly or in small clusters in other tissues.
